issues.title: [Performance] Track device-backed FEX, Wine and Metal optimization work
issues.body:
## Goal and evidence

Coordinate the first device-backed performance work in **brookesdjb/Madeira only**. The investigation is on [investigation/performance-2026-10-10](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/tree/investigation/performance-2026-10-10/docs/performance-investigation), pinned at `c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e`; audited runtime source is `48f976429c189f8396e23d251d8a82f43c705922`.

Read [recommendations](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/recommendations.md), [architecture](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/architecture.md), and [benchmark protocol](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/benchmark-plan.md). Source-backed findings are not measured iPad speedups. C = confirmed source work, S = supported opportunity, H = profiling hypothesis.

## First dispatch wave

Child issue links will be added after creation: device baseline/telemetry, X1 diagnostic gates, G1 cache persistence, W1 wake coalescing, G2 compiler-worker experiment, and F2 JIT block-size experiment.

Development can start independently; final performance acceptance requires the baseline and a physical iPad. X1 must be controlled identically in both arms of later experiments.

## Agent workflow and shared-device ownership

- One issue, dedicated git worktree/branch, isolated DerivedData/build/staging paths, and one reviewable PR. Do not overwrite shared native archives or DLL farms.
- Record base SHA, submodule pins, installed binary hashes, effective settings and changed files. Re-read applicable AGENTS.md and current code before implementing: source may have advanced.
- Coordinate overlapping files (notably WineProcessBridge.m and server_ios.c). Agree instrumentation ownership rather than independently adding incompatible telemetry.
- The baseline issue must establish a **single shared device reservation** used by every agent. Hold it from install through JIT activation, gameplay, capture, cleanup and thermal recovery; identify owner/run and recover stale ownership explicitly.
- Only one agent may install, launch, interact with or benchmark on the iPad at a time. Do not replace another run's app, reset caches, touch game saves, or steal a live reservation.
- Serialize performance captures and avoid competing Mac builds during captures. Parallel source work/host tests can proceed in isolated worktrees.
- Keep separate cold/disk-warm/process-warm captures. Use repeated paired AB/BA runs and sustained thermal trials; one variable per experiment.
- Every PR needs mechanism evidence, raw captures/run manifest, correctness results, rollback instructions and remaining limitations. Negative experiments are useful; do not promote a new default without benefit.
- No blanket TSO disablement, skipped instruction-cache flushes, unsafe fence modes, unproven lock removal or reuse of GPU-live memory.
- **FEX/AGENTS.md prohibits AI-generated code contributions.** F2 is a Madeira configuration experiment, not permission to edit FEX. FEX implementation candidates need a maintainer-compatible route.
- Fork issues authorize work planning; they do not require publishing changes to original upstream repositories or silently merging other experimental branches.

## Deferred backlog — profile before promoting to implementation

The pinned recommendations document contains complete locations, proposals, effort/risk and validation for all 23 candidates. Preserve these as deferred planning items, not asserted bugs:

- W3 fastsync spin/park/fallback policy; X2 selective app optimization and Release failure isolation.
- F1 diagnostic counter overhead; W2 active descriptor scans; G7 idle cache eviction.
- G4 resource copies/Map waits; X3 alias/exception faults; G3 durable PSO archives.
- G5 D3D12 per-PSO dependency graph; F3 duplicate JIT compilation; F4 JIT/cache memory budgets.
- W6 role scheduling; X4 shared memory budgets; W4 madsync lock sharding; W5 pseudo-process context isolation.
- G6 heaps/formats; F5 translated/native transitions; F6 persistent JIT data cache.

Create a dedicated follow-up issue only when its measurement gate and ownership are clear.

## Completion

The first wave is complete when each child has an evidence-backed disposition (land, reject, or explicitly defer), linked PR/results, and the recommendations are updated with actual physical-device findings. No performance gain is assumed in advance.

issues.title: [Performance][Baseline] Establish physical-iPad captures and shared-device reservation
issues.body:
## Objective

Create a reproducible physical M-series iPad performance baseline and reusable low-overhead measurements. This is measurement infrastructure, not a claim of speedup.

## Dependencies and starting points

A provisioned Mac, Xcode/toolchains, connected iPad, working app launch and JIT are required for device acceptance. Inspect the existing [automation branch status](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/4bcf62af564cb7c58c752429e783a96872609134/docs/automation/implementation-status.md) before duplicating its Appium/devicectl controller; it does not establish physical JIT coexistence. Coordinate with that work and do not merge it blindly.

Read [benchmark plan](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/benchmark-plan.md). Start from the native Present/command-queue boundaries described in [DXMT](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/dxmt.md), Wine server_call_unlocked and diagnostic sites in [Wine](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/wine.md), and existing offline tools in the investigation directory. Do not treat aggregate overlay FPS as recoverable per-frame samples.

## Scope

1. Document exact build/sign/install/JIT launch commands on the actual Mac, installed binary hashes, pins and effective configuration.
2. Establish a shared device reservation visible to every agent: atomic acquisition, owner/run identity, guaranteed cleanup and explicit stale-owner recovery. Cover install, JIT, gameplay, capture and thermal recovery. Verify a second client cannot take a live reservation.
3. Add or reuse opt-in, release-disabled low-overhead raw frame export and per-role CPU measurements. Separate Metal encoding/submission CPU from GPU timestamps; correlate command buffers to rendered frames. Keep missing quantities explicitly missing.
4. Coordinate telemetry with X1 so diagnostics are controlled and observer overhead measured. No hot-path synchronous logging, unbounded allocation or unsafe exception-handler work.
5. Run one CPU-heavy x64, x86/D3D9, D3D11 streaming/shader, and D3D12 case where installed games support them. Record unavailable cases rather than invent coverage.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Repeatable actual device launch/JIT/game/capture/cleanup, with errors recorded and bounded retries.
- [ ] Shared reservation excludes a competing client and safely releases after failure.
- [ ] Saved source/binary/config/device/OS/game/scene/thermal manifests; no credentials or private identifiers in published artifacts.
- [ ] Raw rendered-frame intervals and documented CPU/GPU attribution; counter accuracy and enabled/disabled overhead checked.
- [ ] At least five paired 180-second runs after 60-second settling for a repeatable scene, plus a 15-minute sustained trial, or explicit evidence-backed blocked status.
- [ ] Cold, disk-warm and process-warm states separated; p50/p95/p99, over-budget frames, load time, footprint and variability reported.
- [ ] Reproducible commands and artifacts linked for the five optimization issues; no simulator timings labeled as iPad results.

Effort: medium; compatibility risk: low–medium due to instrumentation/lifecycle; owner: Madeira/harness. This issue does not authorize broad runtime refactoring.

## Agent execution and landing requirements

Use the performance tracking issue's shared-device reservation, separate worktree/build outputs and PR rules. This issue supplies the baseline needed for the optimization issues; host-only preparation may start before device access. Keep X1 sampler policy identical across comparison arms. Re-read current source and applicable AGENTS.md; documentation pins describe the audited baseline, not necessarily today's checkout.

Use one-variable paired AB/BA runs, separate cold/warm phases, raw frame data, per-role CPU/GPU attribution, load time and 15-minute thermal/memory trials. Preserve source/binary/config manifests. A successful build or host model is not a measured device speedup. Record negative results and retain current defaults when benefit is unproven.

Submit a dedicated PR to brookesdjb/Madeira with implementation rationale, meaningful correctness tests, device evidence, limitations and rollback. Do not publish upstream or merge unrelated branches as part of this issue.

References: [recommendations](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/recommendations.md), [benchmark plan](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/benchmark-plan.md), [architecture](https://github.com/brookesdjb/Madeira/blob/c2f0b67e8b27b83220cdff221107fe66c3d7502e/docs/performance-investigation/architecture.md). ## Scope and evidence

| Field | Recommendation |

| Subsystem | DXMT / integration |

issues.title: [Performance][W1] coalesce wineserver request wakeups
issues.body:
## Scope and evidence

| Field | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Subsystem | Wine |
| Finding and evidence | S: signal once per request and consume once per loop pass; multiple requests can be drained in one scan, leaving wake-token backlog and extra scans |
| Code location | `ios_wineserver_wake`, [build/wineserver/fd_ios.c:34–47](https://github.com/willfaust/Madeira/blob/48f976429c189f8396e23d251d8a82f43c705922/build/wineserver/fd_ios.c#L34-L47); iOS `main_loop` wake wait [build/wineserver/fd_ios.c:1390–1468](https://github.com/willfaust/Madeira/blob/48f976429c189f8396e23d251d8a82f43c705922/build/wineserver/fd_ios.c#L1390-L1468); client [build/ntdll-unix/server_ios.c:1841–1861](https://github.com/willfaust/Madeira/blob/48f976429c189f8396e23d251d8a82f43c705922/build/ntdll-unix/server_ios.c#L1841-L1861) |
| Proposed code change | Atomic pending/sequence protocol: publish request then signal only on transition to pending; server clears before draining, handles races and leaves a wake for post-scan work. Preserve timer/INET deadline and explicit stop wake. Keep existing path behind a rollback switch |
| Why it helps | Fewer Mach semaphore signals and unproductive full descriptor scans without delaying actual work |
| Performance potential | Medium, potentially high in server-heavy bursts; no expected help for pure GPU-bound frames |
| Implementation effort / compatibility risk | Medium / medium; lost wakeups and timeout regressions are central risks |
| Validation | Adversarial clear/scan/sleep interleavings, request/scan ratios, p99 round trip, network progress and quit under load; don't accept the timer rescuing missed signals |
| Upstream dependency | None outside Madeira native Wine overlay; do not parallelize server handlers |

issues.title: [Performance][G2] budget shader compiler workers
issues.body:
## Scope and evidence

| Field | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Subsystem | DXMT / scheduling |
| Finding and evidence | H: task scheduler can grow to 2×hardware concurrency, competing with game/FEX/encode/audio work; first-use callers still wait for pipelines |
| Code location | `task_scheduler` constructor/worker/submit, [dxmt/src/dxmt/dxmt_tasks.hpp:48–79](https://github.com/willfaust/dxmt/blob/db546ee466ad50ec6463edb5fa183de11db43761/src/dxmt/dxmt_tasks.hpp#L48-L79), [dxmt/src/dxmt/dxmt_tasks.hpp:131–146](https://github.com/willfaust/dxmt/blob/db546ee466ad50ec6463edb5fa183de11db43761/src/dxmt/dxmt_tasks.hpp#L131-L146); `GetPipeline`, [dxmt/src/d3d11/d3d11_pipeline.cpp:49–56](https://github.com/willfaust/dxmt/blob/db546ee466ad50ec6463edb5fa183de11db43761/src/d3d11/d3d11_pipeline.cpp#L49-L56) |
| Proposed code change | Add a validated optional compiler-worker cap and active/queued/completion telemetry. Start A/B at caps 2 and 4 versus existing policy; retain existing default until measured. Preserve continuation scheduling and avoid forcing compiler/finish workers to highest QoS as a general policy |
| Why it helps | Can reduce oversubscription, priority competition and heat while allowing the render/encode critical path to run |
| Performance potential | Medium, conditional; fewer workers can also increase loading time |
| Implementation effort / compatibility risk | Medium / medium; starvation/dependency liveness and resource ownership must stay correct |
| Validation | Cold and warm p99 plus load time, compiler queue length, per-role CPU, input/audio and 15-minute thermals across two iPads |
| Upstream dependency | DXMT iOS fork; generic scheduler option could be offered upstream |

issues.title: [Performance][F2] make JIT block-size tuning a bounded per-game experiment
issues.body:
## Scope and evidence

| Field | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| Subsystem | FEX / Madeira configuration |
| Finding and evidence | H: default multiblock maximum 5,000 instructions can trade warm dispatch efficiency for cold compile latency; no optimal iPad value has been measured here |
| Code location | FEX defaults [FEX/FEXCore/Source/Interface/Config/Config.json.in:1–18](https://github.com/willfaust/FEX/blob/3bec2ac498bf78156ab47c0c194b0e8cb2849756/FEXCore/Source/Interface/Config/Config.json.in#L1-L18); generation/pass call [FEX/FEXCore/Source/Interface/Core/Core.cpp:1174–1243](https://github.com/willfaust/FEX/blob/3bec2ac498bf78156ab47c0c194b0e8cb2849756/FEXCore/Source/Interface/Core/Core.cpp#L1174-L1243); app config export in `WineProcessBridge.m` around 1140 |
| Proposed code change | Add a diagnostic per-game choice to Madeira's existing config/profile flow, validating {500,1000,5000} and exporting `FEX_MAXINST` before translator initialization. Log the effective value; require fresh app launch. Reuse raw `env.FEX_MAXINST` first; no FEX implementation change is needed for the experiment |
| Why it helps | If cold compilation causes frame spikes, smaller regions may reduce pause size; a warmed region may instead lose efficiency, so promote only demonstrated per-game settings |
| Performance potential | Medium for compilation stutter, unknown or negative for warm throughput |
| Implementation effort / compatibility risk | Low for controlled config / medium because Mono/invalidation behaviors depend on translation shape |
| Validation | Exact instruction/FP/exception tests and representative Mono games; compile-duration distribution, emitted bytes, dispatch misses, cold/warm frame tails |
| Upstream dependency | Madeira-only experiment; adaptive block formation would require FEX development and its contribution policy |
